name: Devyani International Ltd
title: Devyani International Ltd - 543330 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: QSR franchisee Devyani posted record Q1 FY27 EBITDA of INR 255 crore (16.1% of revenue on its KFC/own-brand basis per call), with KFC SSSG +3.3% but Pizza Hut still shrinking (-2.2%) and no capex or capacity signal; supply-side read is neutral with store additions modest at 11 net KFC.

capex.quote: Not much change in capex, so whatever format we are opening currently, that is what is going to be happening for future also.

triggers.label: KFC ADS threshold 105k-110k for 20% margin
triggers.quote: once we cross a threshold of 105,000 ADS to 110,000 ADS, we will be able to cross 20% Brand Contribution margins in KFC

triggers.label: KFC SSSG +3.3% in Q1
triggers.quote: another positive SSSG of 3.3% during the quarter

triggers.label: Slight price increases at KFC and Pizza Hut
triggers.quote: We have taken slight price increases in KFC and Pizza Hut to mitigate the cost impact

triggers.label: Pizza Hut SSSG -2.2%, ADS ~INR 32,400
triggers.quote: SSSG came in at minus 2.2%, improving sequentially, with an uptick in ADS to ~INR 32,400 per store per day

guidance.quote: we are looking at a SSSG of about 5% to 6% for KFC
our target remains to get to a number of 59%-60%
we continue to expect completion of the merger by end of the current financial year

guidance.value: INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years
guidance.quote: our objective is to make sure that this brand gets to INR 1,000 crore brand in the next few years

red_flags.quote: SSSG came in at minus 2.2%, improving sequentially

red_flags.label: Brand Contribution loss at Pizza Hut
red_flags.quote: Pizza Hut posted a Brand Contribution loss of INR 4 crore.

evasions.quote: So obviously, that will get corrected as the structure kind of eases out when we get the merger approval.
Q2, it is too early to say because we are still in the month of July.

summary.headline: Devyani Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore, with record Operating EBITDA of INR 151 crore (9.6% margin).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.5% YoY to INR 1,581 crore and Operating EBITDA rose about 38% YoY to INR 151 crore, the company's highest ever, at a 9.6% margin. KFC returned to positive SSSG (3.3%) with dine-in salience improving to 57%, while Pizza Hut remained loss-making at brand contribution level with SSSG of -2.2%. Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a weak monsoon outlook and volatile macro, and said Sapphire merger approvals from NSE and BSE were received in June with completion targeted by end FY27.

segments.name: KFC India
segments.commentary: SSSG +3.3%, revenue INR 684 crore (~+12% YoY), gross margin 69.4%, brand contribution INR 115 crore; offline saliency 57%, up over 3 pp YoY. Management targets 59-60% dine-in share and ADS of 105k-110k for 20%+ brand contribution margin.

segments.name: Pizza Hut
segments.commentary: SSSG -2.2% (improving sequentially), ADS up to ~INR 32,400 per store per day, revenue INR 184 crore, gross margin 76.3%, brand contribution loss INR 4 crore; 626 stores at quarter end.

segments.name: Own brands (BBK, Vaango)
segments.commentary: Biryani By Kilo SSSG +7.2%, Vaango +7.1%; combined revenue INR 98 crore, gross margin 65.9%, brand contribution ~INR 10 crore (10.2%). 218 stores including 23 BBK Express; BBK target INR 1,000 crore brand in next few years.

segments.name: Franchise brands (incl. Costa)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~6% YoY; gross margin fell to 74.6% on input costs; brand contribution margin 15.1%, up YoY on cost management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 523 crore, growth above 20% YoY for another quarter; brand contribution margin 18.2%, up 1.5 pp YoY.

guidance_outlook: KFC SSSG expected around 5-6% over the medium term per management; Percy Panthaki's follow-up framed 105k-110k ADS as roughly 1.5-2 years away on that basis.
Brand contribution margin for KFC to cross 20% once ADS passes 105k-110k; management said this is conditional on the current cost environment.
Store opening plan unchanged from earlier guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1; 1,855 stores in India and 2,255 globally at June 30, 2026.
Merger with Sapphire Foods expected to complete by end FY27; management said Pizza Hut's full focus would come after the merger, which Vivek Maheshwari confirmed as FY28.
Early Q2 trends: July showed positive trend per management, but Shravan timing creates a drag; Q2 is too early to call.
capex_capacity: Store opening pace in line with prior guidance; 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1.
Management said there is spare capacity in existing KFC stores, so the dine-in shift needs no additional capex; future formats will stay as currently sized.
BBK Express small-box format (23 stores) being tested in food courts; BBK dine-in and airport formats being piloted.
Technology platform build: core team in-house with outsourcing to Cognizant; tech rollout targeted before merger approval.
demand_pricing: KFC SSSG +3.3%; management reports demand 'stable' and July trends positive, but macro (LPG, rupee, crude) remains a constraint.
Slight price increases taken at KFC and Pizza Hut to offset LPG and commodity costs; KFC gross margin restored to 69.4% through judicious discounting.
KFC marketing rebalanced from deep online discounting toward dine-in visits.
Pizza Hut ADS is low versus peers; management says innovation and price laddering across price points are needed, with product work ongoing.
Franchise brands gross margin fell to 74.6% on higher input costs, offset by better cost management.

qa_highlights.question: What drivers beyond SSSG could lift KFC margins from ~17% and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the key lever is ADS; crossing 105k-110k ADS should take KFC brand contribution above 20%. Other levers are dine-in promotion, operating leverage and technology adoption, which will only deliver a few quarters after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: Can KFC dine-in salience return to 60-65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65% is not achievable near term given convenience preference, especially in the North; the target is 59-60%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SSSG not guided higher after 13 quarters of negative trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited tough macro (rupee, oil, LPG availability) and said a bullish view needs a stable environment that it does not yet see.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Pizza Hut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 3-way structure with Sapphire and Yum! held back decisions and innovation; product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway, with full push after the merger.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mandate and leadership build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters are supportive on investment; new COO, CTO and CMO have been hired, with joinings ranging from 2 weeks to 2 months; the whole leadership team is now in place.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Sapphire integration be straightforward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IT stacks and processes are largely similar because technology was run by Yum!, so integration should not be a major challenge.

risks_watch: Inflation in LPG, wages, food commodities and packaging could offset the KFC margin path; management said the ADS target may move if costs rise.
Below-normal monsoon forecast and El Niño risk could weigh on demand.
Pizza Hut remains loss-making at brand contribution level with ADS well below peers.
Merger completion by end FY27 and the technology build-out being ready before merger approval.
Aggregator dynamics and delivery cannibalising dine-in sales; management is shifting marketing toward dine-in.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and KFC momentum, but cautious on macro, SSSG outlook and Pizza Hut; management repeatedly said it is too early to call Q2 and that a bullish view requires macro stability.
key_quotes: The business has improved profitability and posted its highest ever EBITDA of INR 255 crore at 16.1% of the revenues.

So the key lever for ADS, as you know, is a combination of SSSG in the existing stores, as well as the quality of new stores that we are opening, so that we are able to start the new stores at a higher ADS number.

So, Vivek, this hypothesis used to play when delivery was new, and I am talking about, let us say, post-COVID period, because that was giving us net addition in terms of top line, and on an incremental basis, it made sense .
Today, we have excess capacity available in our stores, whereby we can easily make the shift without incurring additional capex.

adds.what: 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in India in Q1 FY27 (1,855 India stores, 2,255 globally at June 30, 2026)
BBK Express small-box format (23 stores) being tested in food courts; BBK dine-in and airport formats being piloted

growth.why: Management guides KFC SSSG of about 5-6% medium term and a 20%+ KFC brand contribution margin once ADS reaches 105k-110k (roughly 1.5-2 years away), backed by Q1 store additions (11 KFC, 3 BBK) and a dine-in shift using existing spare capacity, but no specific new capacity or order numbers beyond the store plan, so backing is partial.

mgmt.note: Vivek Maheshwari confirmed Pizza Hut's full focus will come after the Sapphire merger, framed as FY28; no change in top management was described in the brief.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: KFC brand contribution rose about 22% with margin up 1.4 pp, consolidated Operating EBITDA hit a record INR 151 crore (9.6% margin, +38% YoY), and KFC brand contribution is guided above 20% once ADS reaches 105k-110k, roughly 1.5-2 years away, conditional on costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Store additions continue at pace: 11 net new KFC and 3 net new BBK stores in Q1 FY27, taking India stores to 1,855 and global to 2,255, though management said future formats stay as currently sized with no major new capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: KFC SSSG of +3.3% with July trends positive, store additions of 11 KFC and 3 BBK in Q1, and International revenue growing above 20% YoY to INR 523 crore; Pizza Hut ADS is still low at about INR 32,400 per store per day.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said capex is not changing and spare capacity exists in existing KFC stores, so the dine-in shift needs no additional capex; no utilisation figure was disclosed to support a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management refused to guide SSSG above the 5-6% medium-term range and said a bullish view needs a stable macro it does not yet see; KFC SSSG was +3.3% in Q1 after 13 quarters of negative trends.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged LPG, wage and commodity inflation, a below-normal monsoon and El Nino risk, and said the ADS target may move if costs rise; Q2 is too early to call and Shravan timing is a drag.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pizza Hut product, ingredient and price-ladder work is underway with full push after the merger (FY28), and BBK Express, dine-in and airport formats are in trials with 23 BBK Express stores; no firm launch dates were given.

rows.label: Sapphire Foods merger completion
rows.why: NSE and BSE approvals received in June and management continues to expect completion by end of FY27; Pizza Hut's full focus is set for FY28 after the merger.

rows.label: BBK brand scale-up to INR 1,000 crore
rows.why: Own brands revenue is INR 98 crore in Q1 with BBK SSSG +7.2% and 218 stores; the INR 1,000 crore ambition is a multi-year objective with no interim timeline.

rows.label: Dine-in shift and marketing rebalancing at KFC
rows.why: KFC dine-in salience rose to 57% (up over 3 pp YoY) with a 59-60% target, and marketing is moving away from deep online discounting, supporting KFC brand contribution margin.

tone.note: Management was confident on record EBITDA, KFC's return to positive SSSG and the merger timeline, but cautious on macro, the 5-6% SSSG path and Pizza Hut, and analysts pushed on SSSG and ADS timing.
